summary.short: Pending New York bill (print S1169-B) adding Civil Rights Law article 10-A: developers and deployers of high-risk AI used for consequential decisions must prevent algorithmic discrimination, notify people, offer appeals with human review, commission audits, report to DFS and keep risk programs. Bans social scoring. Effective one year after enactment.
summary.long: S1169-B, the New York artificial intelligence act, would add article 10-A to the Civil Rights Law. It covers developers and deployers that do business in New York or target New York residents; state agencies, local governments and public universities are excluded. Failing to take reasonable care against foreseeable algorithmic discrimination from a high-risk AI system becomes an unlawful discriminatory practice, also added to Executive Law section 296. High-risk systems are a substantial factor in consequential decisions on employment, education, housing, family planning, health care, financial or legal services, or materially affect rights or safety. Covered deployers must notify people before and within ten days after such decisions, offer an appeal with meaningful human review answered within 45 days, and have a human review each decision. Covered developers and deployers must commission recurring independent audits (ISO 42001 audits count; in-house auditors allowed if a compliant audit costs over 1% of fair market value), file periodic reports with the Department of Financial Services, keep a risk management program and protect whistleblowers. Social scoring is banned; the Attorney General can seek injunctions and civil penalties up to $25,000 per violation for developers and $10,000 for deployers. Audits start two years after enactment.

territorial_scope.description: New York State; reaches developers and deployers that do business in New York or whose products or services target New York residents, wherever located. State and local government bodies and public universities are excluded.

evidence.quote: This article applies to developers and deployers that conduct business in New York or produce products or services that are targeted to residents of New York.

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health
agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

evidence.quote: An employee harmed by a violation of this article may petition a court for appropriate relief as provided in subdivision five of section seven hundred forty of the labor law
"Algorithmic discrimination" means any condition in which the use of an AI system contributes to unjustified differential treatment or impacts

"Artificial intelligence system" or "AI system" means a machine-based system or combination of systems, that for a given set of human-defined objectives, makes predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments
"Auditor" shall refer to an independent entity including but not limited to an individual, non-profit, firm, corporation

"Consequential decision" means a decision or judgment that has a material, legal or similarly significant effect on an individual's access to, or the cost, terms, or availability of, any of the following
"Covered deployer" means a deployer that uses a high-risk AI system to make one or more consequential decisions with respect to covered subjects.

"Deployer" means any person, partnership, association or ... that uses or makes an AI system available to one or more third parties including the general public ... A deployer shall not include any natural person using an AI system for personal use.
"Covered developer" means a developer that trained or initiated the training of an AI system that is used to make one or more consequential decisions with respect to covered subjects.

"Developer" means a person, partnership, or corporation that trained or initiated the training of an AI system, or creates a ... whether for its own use in the state of New York or for use by a third party
"Employee" means an individual who performs services for and under the control and direction of an employer for wages or other

"Covered agent" means any individual that interacts, directly or indirectly, with a relevant AI system, developer, or deployer on behalf of a covered subject with the express consent of such covered subject.
"Covered subject" means any individual or group of individuals that is the subject of a consequential decision made entirely by or with the assistance of an AI system.
"Fair market value" shall have the same meaning as such term is defined in 20 NYCRR 3-2.3.

"High-risk AI system" means any AI system that, when deployed: (a) is a substantial factor in making a consequential decision; or (b) will have a material impact on the statutory or constitutional rights, civil liberties, safety, or welfare of an individual in the state.
"ISO 42001" means international standard ISO/IEC 42001:2023 (Information technology -- Artificial intelligence -- Management system)
"Substantial change" means any new version, new release, or any other intentional update to an AI system that results in significant and material changes to such AI system's appropriate use cases
"Substantial factor" means a factor that is (a) material in making a consequential decision, or (b) is capable of altering the outcome of a consequential decision.

"Meaningful human review" shall mean review, oversight and control of the AI system by one or more individuals who understand the risks, limitations, and functionality of, and are trained to use, the AI system

notes: Legislative history: the Assembly record also shows '01/07/2026 died in assembly' and 'returned to senate' (end of the 2025 session year; the bill carried over and was re-referred to Internet and Technology); the vocabulary has no event type for this, so it is recorded here. No Assembly action on the B print appears after delivery on 2026-06-03. Text issues: § 110(3)(a) reads 'thirty-party auditors' (apparently 'third-party'); § 112(1) refers to 'subdivision one of section one hundred six', but § 106 has no subdivisions. Enforcement gaps as written: § 114(1) lists violations of §§ 107, 108, 110, 111, 112 and 113 for Attorney General injunctions, so § 106 (the discrimination duty) is enforced through Executive Law § 296(23) and § 109 through Labor Law § 740; § 114(3) gives the supreme court jurisdiction over 'any action, claim, or lawsuit' to enforce the article, without expressly creating a private right of action. § 108(3) makes covered deployers and developers 'legally responsible' for the quality and accuracy of consequential decisions (coded as liability_rule). § 107(2) excludes state agencies, local governments, SUNY, CUNY and community colleges. Auditors are themselves bound by § 110(7) (no fully AI-made audits). The Attorney General may also make discretionary rules on audits and auditor independence (§ 110(5), (8)) and choose an alternative risk framework (§ 112(1)(a)(iii)). Civil penalties under § 114(1) are coded sanction_type 'other' because the vocabulary has no court-imposed civil-penalty type.
